calls.user: Question: explain data engineering in simple words Passages: [Ch. 4] chunk_id=ch04-001 Chapter 4. Choosing Technologies Across the Data Engineering Lifecycle Data engineering nowadays suffers from an embarrassment of riches. We have no shortage of technologies to solve various types of data problems. Data technologies are available as turnkey offerings consumable in almost every way—open source, managed open source, proprietary software, proprietary service, and more. However, it’s easy to get caught up in chasing bleeding-edge technology while losing sight of the core purpose of data engineering: designing robust and reliable systems to carry data through the full lifecycle and serve it according to the needs of end users. Just as structural engineers carefully choose technologies and materials to realize an architect’s vision for a building, data engineers are tasked with making appropriate technology choices to shepherd data through the lifecycle to serve data applications and users. Chapter 3 discussed “good” data architecture and why it matters. We now explain how to choose the right technologies to serve this architecture. Data engineers must choose good technologies to make the best possible data product. We feel the criteria to choose a good data technology is simple: does it add value to a data product and the broader business? We define data engineering and data engineer as follows: Data engineering is the development, implementation, and maintenance of systems and processes that take in raw data and produce high-quality, consistent information that supports downstream use cases, such as analysis and machine learning. Data engineering is the intersection of security, data management, DataO
calls.out: Data engineering involves developing, implementing, and maintaining systems and processes that handle raw data, transforming it into high-quality, consistent information for use by data scientists, analysts, and other stakeholders [Ch. 1]. It encompasses the movement, manipulation, and management of data [Ch. 1], and is the intersection of security, data management, DataOps, data architecture, orchestration, and software engineering [Ch. 1]. The core purpose is to design robust and reliable systems to carry data through its lifecycle and serve it according to end-user needs [Ch. 4]. Data engineers ensure data remains available and usable, setting up and operating the organization’s data infrastructure [Ch. 1].
